name: MonarchChatDock
title: ChatDock
summary: A floating chat launcher with an unread count; a tap opens the chat in a sheet that stops at half height, so the screen behind stays visible and usable, and pulls up to full height.
whenToUse: In a product app that offers its team chat from every screen without leaving the current task.
whenNotToUse: For the chat app itself, build the screens from the collaboration components in a NavigationSplitView. For one conversation about a record, use MonarchThreadPanel or MonarchCommentThread.
api: init(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, unread: Int = 0, title: String? = nil, unreadLabel: String? = nil, @ViewBuilder chat: () -> Chat)

options.name: isPresented
options.description: Whether the chat sheet is open.

options.name: unread
options.description: The unread count shown as a badge; above 99 it shows "99+".

options.name: unreadLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken value "%d unread"; %d stands for the number.

options.name: chat
options.description: The chat view shown in the sheet.

states.name: closed
states.description: A 48-point rounded launcher on the inverse background with a speech bubble, and a danger badge when there are unread messages.

states.name: open
states.description: A sheet at half height with a drag indicator; the screen behind stays interactive. It can be pulled to full height.

appearance: The launcher uses the inverse background and inverse text colour with a medium shadow; the badge uses the danger solid colour. The sheet uses the surface colour. Colours come from theme roles in every theme.
platformNotes: The web ChatDock keeps the Rook Chat web app alive in an iframe behind its launcher, with a postMessage contract for sessions, unread counts and incoming calls. On iOS the chat is the app's own view in a system sheet; its state lives in the app's model because a sheet's view is rebuilt each time it opens, and the unread count is passed in. Incoming-call prompts are not part of the dock: calls use CallKit. Android does not ship this component.
accessibility: The launcher is a button named "Rook Chat" (or title) with the value "3 unread".
The badge is drawn only; the count is read as the launcher's value.
The sheet has the system drag indicator and closes with the standard gestures and the Escape key.
The launcher scales with Dynamic Type and is larger than 44 points.
edgeCases: Place the launcher above the tab bar with .padding or .safeAreaInset so it does not cover it.
At full height the sheet covers the screen; the medium detent keeps the screen usable.
